title: Injectivity criterion for finitely presented modules over a local essentially finitely presented algebra
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m_R)$ and $(S,\mathfrak m_S)$ be commutative local rings, and let $R\to S$ be a local homomorphism. Assume that $S$ is essentially of finite presentation over $R$, meaning that there are a finitely presented $R$-algebra $P$, a multiplicative subset $W\subseteq P$, and an isomorphism of $R$-algebras $S\cong W^{-1}P$. Let $M$ and $N$ be finitely presented $S$-modules [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], let $u:M\to N$ be an $S$-linear map, assume $N$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and assume that the induced map $M/\mathfrak m_RM\to N/\mathfrak m_RN$ is injective. Then $u$ is injective and $N/u(M)$ is flat over $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), statement and proof at lines 32770--32848

proof.text: Apply simultaneous Noetherian approximation to $R\to S$, $M,N,u$. Obtain one directed system $R_i\to S_i$, modules $M_i,N_i$ and maps $u_i$, with local transitions and cocones, algebraic ring/group colimits, and the transition and limit localization and module base-change identifications. In particular both $R_i$ and $S_i$ are Noetherian, $M_i,N_i$ are finite, and every comparison carries the stage map to the later map. The approximation lemma requires neither flatness nor fibre injectivity, so all its hypotheses come directly from the statement.

source.place: Tag 046Y, first proof paragraph; Tags 00QV/00QX simultaneous presentation construction

proof.text: Apply the residue-tensor comparison lemma to the source diagram from Step 1. Its finite stage modules, essentially finite type stage algebras, local cocones, localized ring transitions, module base-change identifications and algebraic colimits are all supplied by approximation. Writing $k=R/\mathfrak m_R$ and $k_i=R_i/\mathfrak m_i$, obtain $i_1$ such that $\Psi_j$ is injective for all $j\ge i_1$; by the explicit isomorphisms of that lemma, this is injectivity of $(M_j/\mathfrak m_jM_j)\otimes_{k_j}k\to M/\mathfrak m_RM$, $[x]\otimes[r]\mapsto[r\mu_j(x)]$, the comparison map hypothesized in Step 3.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), middle proof paragraph, construction of the Noetherian residue-tensor diagram and stabilization of its comparison kernels; old steps 3--5.

proof.text: Apply the Noetherian arrow-stage lemma to the same approximation and $i_1$. Both stage rings are Noetherian and both stage modules are finite; all required local maps, commuting arrow squares, localized base-change transitions and ring/group colimits come from Step 1. The limit target $N$ is $R$-flat and $\overline u$ is injective by hypothesis; Step 2 supplies its remaining comparison hypothesis. Thus at every $j$ in a common tail, $u_j$ is injective and $C_j=N_j/u_j(M_j)$ is flat over $R_j$.

source.place: Tag 046Y (lemma-mod-injective-general), first paragraph (eventual target flatness) and final paragraph (faithful field extension, fibre square and stage criterion); Tag 00R6 (lemma-colimit-eventually-flat), Tag 00ME (lemma-mod-injective), and the first proof paragraph of Tag 00MO (lemma-another-variant-local-criterion-flatness); old steps 2, 6, 7.

proof.text: Apply the localized-arrow limit lemma. Step 1 supplies the actual compatible additive colimits, the canonical identifications $M_j\otimes_{S_j}S\cong M$, $N_j\otimes_{S_j}S\cong N$ carrying $u_j\otimes1$ to $u$, and the LIMIT localization $S_j\otimes_{R_j}R\to S$ for every $j$. Step 3 supplies eventual stage injectivity and flat cokernels. The lemma gives injectivity of $u$, its canonical cokernel comparison $C_j\otimes_{S_j}S\cong N/u(M)$, and flatness of $N/u(M)$ over $R$.
